description.narrative: IFC anticipates that the Project will deliver substantial economy-wide benefits and positive impacts for local communities, enhancing fiscal stability, economic performance, and social well-being at both national and regional levels. By supporting Argentinas lithium mining sector in advancing its integration and participation in the global market, the Project is expected to foster market creation and contribute to the affordable energy access and electric mobility. It will employ the innovative Direct Lithium Extraction (DLE) technology, which offers higher yields than conventional evaporation techniques. This will reinforce Argentinas role as a leading global lithium supplier for decades to come. In addition, Rincon is projected to generate economic value for Salta and its stakeholders through local job creation, the development of regional supply chains, and the implementation of community development initiatives.

The Project entails developing, constructing, and operating the greenfield Salar del Rincon battery-grade lithium project (the Project or Rincon). Rincon is expected to produce ~up to 53 thousand tonnes per year (ktpa) of battery-grade Lithium Carbonate Equivalent (LCE) over its 40-year mine. The Project will include wellfields and a brine distribution system, a spent brine disposal facility, a processing complex, filtered waste storage facilities, power transmission lines (two 23 km, 33 kV lines), and ancillary infrastructure.

name.narrative: The project is located on the Salar del Rincon in Salta Province, Argentina, at an altitude of 3,800 meters. It is 1,760km from Buenos Aires and 30km from the Chilean border. The main route to the Project site is from the provincial capital of Salta (approximately 280 km via San Antonio de los Cobres).
